questions.question:
A local Helm chart for the observatory's sky-map frontend is stored at `/home/candidate/exam/q1/orrery` (the chart names its Deployment after the release). In namespace `starmap`, the release `orrery-north` was installed from this chart and then upgraded to an image tag that does not exist, so its new Pods cannot start.

1. Use Helm to roll `orrery-north` back to its last working revision. Afterwards the Deployment `orrery-north` must run image `nginx:1.25` with `2` ready replicas.
2. Write a Helm values file `/home/candidate/exam/q1/south-values.yaml` that sets `replicaCount` to `2` and adds the pod annotation `site: south-ridge` (chart value `podAnnotations`).
3. Install a second release named `orrery-south` from the same local chart into namespace `starmap`, using that values file. Its Deployment `orrery-south` must have `2` ready replicas.

verification.description: orrery-north was rolled back to revision 1 (new revision, status deployed)
Deployment orrery-north runs nginx:1.25 with 2 ready replicas
orrery-south installed from the orrery chart with south-values.yaml (replicaCount 2, podAnnotations.site)
Deployment orrery-south has 2 ready replicas and pod annotation site=south-ridge

questions.question:
In namespace `nightwatch`, the Deployment `watchtower` (2 replicas, label `app=watchtower`, nginx on port `80`) and the Pod `insomniac` are already running.

1. Create a **headless** Service named `watchtower-peers` that selects `app=watchtower` and exposes port `80` (targetPort `80`).
2. From a temporary Pod using image `busybox:1.36`, run `nslookup watchtower-peers.nightwatch.svc.cluster.local` and save the command's output to `/home/candidate/exam/q2/dns.txt`. The output must list the IP address of every `watchtower` Pod. Remove the temporary Pod afterwards.
3. The container of Pod `insomniac` crashed once and was restarted; its current logs look healthy. Save the logs of the **previous** (crashed) container instance, and nothing else, to `/home/candidate/exam/q2/crash.log`.

verification.description: Headless Service watchtower-peers (clusterIP None) selects app=watchtower on port 80 and has 2 endpoints
dns.txt contains the IP of every watchtower Pod
crash.log contains the crashed (previous) container's logs and not the current instance's

questions.question:
Two files have been prepared for the observatory's certificate loader in `/home/candidate/exam/q3/`: `signing.key` and `ca.crt`.

In namespace `vault`:

1. Create a generic Secret named `observatory-tls` from both files, so that it has the keys `signing.key` and `ca.crt` holding the file contents.
2. Create a Pod named `cert-loader` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sh -c 'sleep 3600'`) that:
   - mounts a Secret volume from `observatory-tls` at `/etc/observatory`. The volume must project **only** the key `signing.key`, exposed as the relative path `keys/private.pem` (the file must be `/etc/observatory/keys/private.pem`, and `ca.crt` must not appear in the mount);
   - sets the Secret volume's `defaultMode` to octal `0400`;
   - defines an environment variable `ROTATION_TOKEN` from the key `rotation.token` of Secret `observatory-tls`. That key does not exist yet, so mark the reference as optional: the Pod must still start and be `Running`.

verification.description: Secret observatory-tls has keys signing.key and ca.crt with the file contents
Only signing.key is projected, as keys/private.pem under /etc/observatory
Secret volume defaultMode is 0400 (256) and the key file has mode 400
ROTATION_TOKEN is an optional secretKeyRef to rotation.token and the Pod is Running

questions.question:
In namespace `mirror`, the Deployment `reflector` (3 replicas, container `web`, image `nginx:1.25`) uses the `Recreate` strategy, which takes the site down during every update.

1. Switch the Deployment to the `RollingUpdate` strategy with `maxSurge: 1` and `maxUnavailable: 0`.
2. Update container `web` to image `nginx:1.26`.
3. Set the Deployment annotation `kubernetes.io/change-cause` to `bump reflector to nginx 1.26` so the new revision is described in `kubectl rollout history`.
4. Make sure the rollout completes: `3` replicas, all updated, ready and available, and no Pods left on the old image.

verification.description: Strategy is RollingUpdate with maxSurge=1 and maxUnavailable=0
Container web uses image nginx:1.26
Annotation kubernetes.io/change-cause is 'bump reflector to nginx 1.26'
Rollout complete: 3/3 replicas updated, ready and available on nginx:1.26

questions.question:
In namespace `dome`, the Deployment `skyview` (2 replicas, image `nginx:1.25`, container `web` serving HTTP on port 80) never becomes available: its Pods are Running, but none of them turns Ready because the readiness probe is misconfigured.

Fix the Deployment **in place** (do not delete or recreate it) so that the readiness probe of container `web` performs an HTTP GET on path `/` and port `80`.

Keep every other setting unchanged, including the readiness probe's `initialDelaySeconds: 3`, `periodSeconds: 5` and `failureThreshold: 2`, the existing liveness probe, the image and the replica count. Both replicas must end up Ready.

verification.description: Readiness probe of container web is httpGet on path / and port 80
Deployment fixed in place; replicas, image, probe timings and liveness probe unchanged
2/2 replicas of skyview are updated and Ready

questions.question:
In namespace `relay`, the telemetry `collector` Pods (label `app=collector`) push data to the Redis Pod `archive` (label `app=archive`, TCP port `6379`, Service `archive`). Other Pods such as `webcache` and `dashboard` run in the same namespace.

Create a NetworkPolicy named `collector-egress` in namespace `relay` that selects the Pods labelled `app=collector` (using `matchLabels`) and controls **egress only** (`policyTypes` must be exactly `[Egress]`). The collector Pods may only:
- connect to Pods labelled `app=archive` on TCP port `6379`
- send DNS queries on port `53` over both UDP and TCP (to any destination)

All other outgoing traffic from the collector Pods must be denied. Do not modify the existing Pods, Deployments or Services.

verification.description: collector-egress selects app=collector with policyTypes [Egress]
Egress rule allows Pods app=archive on TCP 6379
Egress allows DNS on port 53 over UDP and TCP
Collector can reach archive:6379 but not webcache:80
Service port 8080 targets the named container port rx-http; Deployment and selector unchanged
Service is NodePort with port 8080 on nodePort 30725
Service has 2 ready endpoints on container port 80

questions.question:
In namespace `calibration`, the Deployment `lens-calibrator` (2 replicas) mounts the ConfigMap `optics-v1` through its volume `optics` at `/etc/lens`.

1. Create a new ConfigMap `optics-v2` that is **immutable** and contains exactly these keys: `FOCAL_LENGTH=2400`, `APERTURE=f11`, `FILTER=h-alpha`.
2. Update the Deployment so that the `optics` volume uses `optics-v2` instead of `optics-v1`. Keep the mount path `/etc/lens` and 2 replicas, and do not modify or delete `optics-v1`.
3. Add the annotation `observatory.io/optics-checksum: 9f2c41ab` to the Deployment's **pod template**.
4. Make sure the rollout completes: both new Pods must be Ready and able to read `/etc/lens/FILTER`.

verification.description: ConfigMap optics-v2 is immutable with exactly FOCAL_LENGTH=2400, APERTURE=f11, FILTER=h-alpha
Deployment lens-calibrator mounts optics-v2 at /etc/lens and no longer references optics-v1
Pod template carries annotation observatory.io/optics-checksum=9f2c41ab
Rollout complete: 2 updated, ready Pods that read FILTER=h-alpha from /etc/lens

questions.question:
Several Pods are running in namespace `survey`. Write two command files. Each file must contain a `kubectl` command, will be executed with `bash <file>`, and must work no matter which namespace is the current default.

1. `/home/candidate/exam/q9/oldest-first.sh`: print only the names of all Pods in namespace `survey`, one per line, sorted by creation time (oldest first). No header and no `pod/` prefix.
2. `/home/candidate/exam/q9/pod-ips.sh`: print all Pods in namespace `survey` using `-o custom-columns` with exactly two columns titled `NAME` (the Pod name) and `POD_IP` (the Pod IP), including the header row.

verification.description: oldest-first.sh prints survey Pod names sorted by creation time
pod-ips.sh prints NAME and POD_IP custom columns for all survey Pods

questions.question:
In namespace `archive`:

1. Create a PersistentVolumeClaim `plate-archive` that requests `100Mi` with access mode `ReadWriteOnce` and uses the StorageClass `local-path` (the default StorageClass, which provisions the volume dynamically).
2. Create a Deployment `plate-scanner` with 1 replica. Its container `scanner` uses image `busybox:1.36`, runs the command `["sh", "-c", "echo scanned-by $(hostname) >> /archive/scans.log; sleep 86400"]` and mounts the PVC at `/archive`.
3. When its Pod is Running, delete that Pod and let the Deployment replace it. The replacement Pod's `/archive/scans.log` must contain its own `scanned-by` line and also the line written by the deleted Pod.

verification.description: PVC plate-archive is Bound, uses StorageClass local-path, requests 100Mi, ReadWriteOnce
Deployment plate-scanner (1 ready replica) mounts PVC plate-archive at /archive in container scanner
The running Pod wrote its own scanned-by line to /archive/scans.log
/archive/scans.log in the running Pod still holds the line of the deleted Pod

questions.question:
In namespace `spectra`, create a Pod named `prism` whose log file is streamed to stdout by a **native sidecar**:

- A volume `logs` of type `emptyDir`, mounted at `/var/log/prism` in both containers below.
- Main container `emitter`, image `busybox:1.36`, running with `sh -c`:
  `i=0; while true; do i=$((i+1)); echo "spectral-line $i" >> /var/log/prism/emission.log; sleep 2; done`
- Sidecar `log-tailer`, image `busybox:1.36`, running with `sh -c`: `tail -F /var/log/prism/emission.log`. It must be declared as a native sidecar, i.e. under `initContainers` with `restartPolicy: Always`.

The Pod must be Running and Ready, and `kubectl logs prism -c log-tailer` must show the `spectral-line` entries.

verification.description: log-tailer is an initContainer with restartPolicy Always (busybox:1.36), emitter is the main container
emptyDir logs is mounted at /var/log/prism in emitter and log-tailer
Pod prism is Running and Ready with the sidecar running
kubectl logs -c log-tailer shows spectral-line entries

questions.question:
Namespace `catalog` contains six star-catalog indexer Pods (`idx-*`) that carry `tier` and `survey` labels and various annotations.

1. On every Pod currently labelled `tier=ingest`, change the value of the label `tier` to `stream`.
2. On every Pod labelled `survey=wide`, add the annotation `catalog.observatory.io/retention` with the exact value `hot=7d,cold=365d`.
3. Write the names of all Pods in the namespace that carry the annotation `catalog.observatory.io/legacy-schema` (whatever its value) to `/home/candidate/exam/q12/legacy-schema-pods.txt`: one Pod name per line, sorted alphabetically, nothing else. Only this exact annotation key counts.

Do not change any other labels or annotations.

verification.description: Former tier=ingest pods now have tier=stream; other tier labels unchanged
Only survey=wide pods carry catalog.observatory.io/retention=hot=7d,cold=365d
legacy-schema-pods.txt lists exactly the pods annotated catalog.observatory.io/legacy-schema, sorted

questions.question:
In namespace `nightly`, create a CronJob named `star-catalog-sync` with these settings:

- schedule `15 3 * * *`, `concurrencyPolicy: Forbid` and `startingDeadlineSeconds: 200`
- created **suspended**, so it does not run until someone resumes it
- a single container `sync` with image `busybox:1.36`, command `["sh", "-c", "echo catalog synced"]` and restartPolicy `OnFailure`
- the container's `securityContext` sets `allowPrivilegeEscalation: false`, drops `ALL` capabilities and uses the `RuntimeDefault` seccomp profile

verification.description: CronJob star-catalog-sync: schedule 15 3 * * *, concurrencyPolicy Forbid, startingDeadlineSeconds 200, container sync busybox:1.36
CronJob is suspended
Container sync: allowPrivilegeEscalation false and capabilities drop ALL
Container sync uses seccompProfile RuntimeDefault

questions.question:
Work in namespace `almanac`.

1. Create a ConfigMap named `sky-settings` from the env-file `/home/candidate/exam/q14/almanac.env`, so that each variable in the file becomes its own key.
2. Create a Pod named `almanac-reader` (image `busybox:1.36`, command `sleep 3600`) that exposes **all** keys of `sky-settings` as environment variables using `envFrom`.
3. Some outdated ConfigMaps in the namespace carry the label `stale=true`. Delete all of them with a single `kubectl delete` that uses a label selector. ConfigMaps without that exact label (for example those labelled `stale=false`) must be kept.

verification.description: ConfigMap sky-settings has one key per env-file variable
Pod almanac-reader loads sky-settings via envFrom
almanac-reader is Running and has all four variables in its environment
All stale=true ConfigMaps deleted, other ConfigMaps kept

questions.question:
In namespace `tracker`, the Deployment `satpos` is already running with memory requests set. A PodDisruptionBudget manifest was left at `/home/candidate/exam/q15/satpos-pdb.yaml`, but it was written for the removed `policy/v1beta1` API and can no longer be applied.

1. Update that file **in place** so it uses the `policy/v1` API (keep the name `satpos-pdb`, `minAvailable: 1` and the selector), then apply it.
2. Create a HorizontalPodAutoscaler named `satpos-hpa` with API `autoscaling/v2` that scales the Deployment `satpos` between `2` and `6` replicas using a single Resource metric: **memory** with an average utilization target of `75` percent. Give it a scale-down behavior with `stabilizationWindowSeconds: 180`.

verification.description: satpos-pdb.yaml uses policy/v1 and is accepted by kubectl
PDB satpos-pdb (policy/v1) has minAvailable 1 and selects app=satpos
HPA satpos-hpa targets Deployment satpos, 2-6 replicas, memory utilization 75%
HPA scaleDown stabilizationWindowSeconds is 180

questions.question:
In namespace `spectro`, the Deployment `prism` should run 3 replicas, but none of its Pods are being created. Find out why.

Fix it without changing the ResourceQuota `spectro-budget` and without adding `resources` to the Deployment:

1. Create a LimitRange `spectro-defaults` of type `Container` with default limits `cpu: 100m`, `memory: 128Mi` and default requests `cpu: 50m`, `memory: 64Mi`.
2. Make sure all 3 replicas of `prism` are Running and Ready with these defaults applied. After many failed attempts the ReplicaSet controller only retries after a long back-off, so restart the Deployment's rollout once the LimitRange exists.

verification.description: LimitRange spectro-defaults sets container defaults (limits 100m/128Mi, requests 50m/64Mi)
Deployment prism has 3/3 ready Pods carrying the LimitRange defaults
prism Pods are admitted while ResourceQuota spectro-budget is unchanged and the Deployment declares no resources

questions.question:
In namespace `orbit`, the Service `telemetry` (selector `app=telemetry`) sends traffic to two Deployments: the stable `telemetry` (3 replicas, `nginx:1.25`) and the canary `telemetry-canary` (1 replica, `nginx:1.26`). The canary has been approved, so promote it:

1. The stable app is managed with Kustomize from `/home/candidate/exam/q17/telemetry/`. Add an `images` entry to its `kustomization.yaml` so that the `nginx` image is rendered with tag `1.26`. Do **not** edit `deployment.yaml` (it must still reference `nginx:1.25`).
2. Apply the directory with `kubectl apply -k` and make sure all 3 replicas of `telemetry` run `nginx:1.26` and are Ready.
3. Delete the Deployment `telemetry-canary`, so that the Service's endpoints are exactly the 3 stable Pods.

verification.description: kustomization.yaml has an images entry; the build renders nginx:1.26 and deployment.yaml is unchanged
Deployment telemetry runs nginx:1.26 with 3/3 updated and Ready replicas
Deployment telemetry-canary and its pods are gone
Service telemetry has exactly 3 endpoints, none from the canary
